items.title: A taut continuous map with dense image out of a complete first countable ring is surjective and open

items.difficulty_reason: Assume a continuous homomorphism of linearly topologized rings is taut with dense image, that the source is complete with a countable fundamental system of open ideals and that the target is separated; the lemma concludes that the map is surjective and open, that the target is complete and that it is a quotient of the source by a closed ideal (statement lines 1454-1465). The proof is displayed in full: the open mapping lemma for linearly topologized rings combined with tautness gives openness, density of the image upgrades openness to surjectivity, continuity makes the kernel closed, and the quotient lemma identifies the target with A/K and yields completeness (proof lines 1468-1476). The level is H2: four short steps, each with its justification named, none of them omitted.
